I've done worse things myself.}} #: {{ux|en|Precisely '''to''' get away from you was why I did what I did.}} #: {{ux|en|I need some more books '''to''' read and friends '''to''' go partying with.}} #: {{ux|en|Those '''to''' avoid death [[ended up]] being exiled.}} #: {{ux|en|He fled to India, never '''to''' return.}} #: {{ux|en|I woke up '''to''' find my name plastered on every [[front page]].}} #: {{ux|en|If he lets you down, he'll have me '''to''' [[reckon with]].}} #* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Criticism|text='''To''' err, is human; '''to''' forgive, divine.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|3|1|text='''To''' be, or not '''to''' be: that is the question: / {{...}}}} #* {{quote-journal |en |date=April 10, 2011 |author=Alistair Magowan |title=Aston Villa 1 - 0 Newcastle |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9446263.stm |page= |passage=To that end, the home supporters were in good voice '''to''' begin with, but it was Newcastle who started the game in the ascendancy, with Barton putting a diving header over the top from Jose Enrique's cross.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903052909/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9446263.stm|archivedate=3 September 2026}} # {{non-gloss|As above, with the verb implied.}} #: {{ux|en|"Did you visit the museum?" "I wanted '''to''', but it was closed."}} #: {{ux|en|If he hasn't read it yet, he ought '''to'''.}} # {{non-gloss|Used to indicate an obligation on the part of, or a directive given to, the subject.}} #: {{ux|en|You are '''to''' go to the store and buy a bottle of milk.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col4|en|{{l|en|finna}} ({{l|en|fixing to}}) |{{l|en|gonna}} ({{l|en|going to}}) |{{l|en|gotta}} ({{l|en|got to}}) |{{l|en|hafta}} ({{l|en|have to}}) |{{l|en|oughta}} ({{l|en|ought to}}) |{{l|en|supposta}} ({{l|en|supposed to}}) |{{l|en|usta}} ({{l|en|used to}}) |{{l|en|wanna}} ({{l|en|want to}}) }} =====Translations===== {{rfc|en|Sense 1 is not the English infinitive morpheme, that would be ''[[-∅]]''. The sentence "I could eat." contains a verb in the infinitive but no ''to''. Rather, ''to'' is a particle that is used in conjunction with an already (zero-)marked infinitive. The box below, however, seems to contain a random mix of translations of the infinitive marker ''[[-∅]]'' (e.g. {{m+|de|-en}}, {{m+|ro|-a}}, {{m+|tr|-mek}}) and the particle ''to'' (e.g. {{m+|de|zu}}, {{m+|ro|a}}).}} {{trans-top|infinitive-marker}}{{multitrans|data= * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Assamese: * Azerbaijani: * Bengali: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Cornish: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Hawaiian: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Igbo: * Indonesian: * Irish: * Italian: * Ladin: * Ladino: * Latin: * Latvian: * Limburgish: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Maltese: * Neapolitan: * Nepali: * Norwegian: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Punjabi: * Romanian: * Russian: {{qualifier|suffix}} {{tt|ru|-ать}}, {{tt|ru|-ять}}, {{tt|ru|-еть}}, {{tt|ru|-ить}}, {{tt+|ru|-ти}}, {{tt|ru|-уть}}, {{tt|ru|-чь}}, {{tt+|ru|-ть}} * Scots: * Serbo-Croatian: * Sicilian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Talysh: * Tamil: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Veps: * Volapük: * Võro: * Votic: * Zulu: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|particle used with infinitives}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * German: {{tt|de|es tun}} {{qualifier|may left out}} * Italian: {{tt+|it|da}} {{qualifier|+ infinitive verb}}, {{tt+|it|per}} {{qualifier|+ infinitive verb}} }} {{trans-bottom}} ====Conjunction==== {{en-head|con}} #
